div.div:
Font lookup: find a font with a glyph for the Unicode code point, using fallback fonts if the primary one lacks it. This is where boxes and � come from.
It queries the operating system's font shaping engine (HarfBuzz / DirectWrite) and requests the vector outline for that character from your active terminal font.

text.tspan: Font lookup: find a font with a glyph for the Unicode code point, using fallback fonts if the primary one
lacks it. This is where boxes and � come from.
It queries the operating system's font shaping engine (HarfBuzz / DirectWrite) and requests the vector
outline for that character from your active terminal font.

text.tspan: The Optimization (Glyph Atlases): Rendering vector outlines for every single character on every frame would
destroy CPU performance. Instead, mordern terminals use a glyph cache. Frequently used characters are
rendered once into a texture atlas (a GPU memory sheet), and the terminal treats them as pre-rendered bitmap
textures

div.div: Programs talk to the terminal through the kernel’s tty API: termios (tcgetattr/tcsetattr) and ioctl. Those calls only succeed on a real tty file descriptor. So the terminal emulator can’t just hand over a pipe and implement the behavior itself, because isatty() would be false and tcsetattr would fail.

text.tspan: Programs talk to the terminal through the kernel’s tty API: termios (tcgetattr/tcsetattr)
and ioctl. Those calls only succeed on a real tty file descriptor. So the terminal
emulator can’t just hand over a pipe and implement the behavior itself, because
isatty() would be false and tcsetattr would fail.
